spec_match.rationale: Compares the actual behaviours the proposal changes — module-map caching vs HTTP caching, rejection vs resolved-404, and the required type attribute proved by importing the text file as JavaScript and getting the MIME refusal.

interactive.rationale: Four buttons each run real network/loader operations and populate measured tables; buttons disable while running and re-enable.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames it as 'when the failure happens, what a second import costs, what the code looks like' and the page delivers precisely those three sections.

edge_cases.rationale: The 404-resolves trap, the no-attribute security refusal, and the unsupported-browser branch all have first-class, accurately narrated paths — including pre-announcing the deliberate console MIME error.

conformance.rationale: The suite's missing-text-module-rejects and cached-by-specifier assertions pin exactly the two behavioural differences this page teaches.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: Run reported the import TypeError honestly with fetch getting 235 chars; second load measured; the missing-file case showed 'import rejected with TypeError' vs 'fetch RESOLVED with status 404 — response.ok had to be checked by hand' (the 404 visible in the network log as intended); the no-attribute import was refused. No unexpected console errors; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each action logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert events (both-loaded, failure-compared, attribute-required) with the relevant flags.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, disabled state styled, good/bad cells use accent colours plus text, tables on paper background.

accessibility.rationale: Real buttons, captioned tables with scoped headers, aria-live outputs for both result areas, and code samples in focusable pre blocks.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; both screenshots clean, buttons wrap on mobile.

openQuestions.title: On a text-modules browser, confirm the second-load claim empirically
openQuestions.detail: The second-load narration asserts the module map 'does no work at all' — on Chrome 155 the measured number should visibly collapse versus the first load, but this branch could not be exercised on Chromium 141 (import fails here). One verification pass on a 155/Canary build should confirm the identical-module fast path and that the 'identical?' column turns yes.

summary: The strongest page in this feature: every claimed difference is executed rather than described, and all four actions were driven over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/import-text-text-modules/fetch-comparison/ — the 404-resolves trap and the no-attribute MIME refusal both reproduced exactly as narrated, with the deliberate 404 and aborted module fetch being the only failed requests, both intended and labelled. Feature /conformance/ route ran 3 pass / 3 fail (honest pre-155 gaps). No overflow on either device class.
